sections.history: Tirunattiyathankudi lies about 14 km from Tiruvarur, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Sundarar, and is honoured as the avatara sthalam — the birthplace — of Kotpuli Nayanar, one of the sixty-three Nayanmars. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later, keeping the form of the Shiva shrines of the Tiruvarur delta.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Rathnapureeswarar — also called Manikkavannar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Maamalar Mangai (also named Ratnapureeswari, Mangalambikai) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas, with a shrine for Kotpuli Nayanar among the saints. The walled courtyard keeps the form of the Tiruvarur delta temples.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Rathnapureeswarar — Manikkavannar, 'the gem-hued lord'; a local account tells of a Chola named Ratnendra who built the temple after the lord divided a hoard of gems fairly between two brothers. Above all the place is remembered as the birthplace of Kotpuli Nayanar, the warrior-saint whose unbending devotion to the service of Shiva is sung among the lives of the sixty-three. The goddess Maamalar Mangai stands beside the lord.
sections.festivals: The temple observes the guru puja of Kotpuli Nayanar, besides Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Tiruvarur delta include Tirunattiyathankudi among their stops, for the Nayanar's sake.
sections.experience: At Tirunattiyathankudi the pilgrim comes to the birthplace of a warrior-saint. Before Rathnapureeswarar and Maamalar Mangai, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the Tiruvarur delta, and the memory of Kotpuli Nayanar, who held the service of Shiva above all else.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirunattiyathankudi lies about 14 km from Tiruvarur, in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur is the nearest town and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
